Are Americans Actually Better Off Than 10 Years Ago?

Simon Zhang

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

economic_data <- read_csv(
  "../data/processed_data/wages_inflation_clean.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

glimpse(economic_data)
Rows: 132
Columns: 7
$ date            <date> 2015-01-01, 2015-02-01, 2015-03-01, 2015-04-01, 2015-05-01, 2015-06-01, 2015-07-01, 2015-08-01, 2015-09-01,…

$ cpi             <dbl> 234.747, 235.342, 235.976, 236.222, 237.001, 237.657, 238.034, 238.033, 237.498, 237.733, 238.017, 237.761, …
$ real_wage       <dbl> 0.1053901, 0.1053361, 0.1053073, 0.1053670, 0.1053582, 0.1050674, 0.1050690, 0.1054476, 0.1057272, 0.1060013…
$ wage_index      <dbl> 98.91714, 99.11705, 99.35695, 99.51688, 99.83674, 99.83674, 99.99667, 100.35651, 100.39649, 100.75634, 100.9…
$ price_index     <dbl> 99.04864, 99.29969, 99.56720, 99.67099, 99.99968, 100.27647, 100.43555, 100.43512, 100.20939, 100.30854, 100…
$ real_wage_index <dbl> 99.86778, 99.81662, 99.78938, 99.84592, 99.83760, 99.56202, 99.56357, 99.92228, 100.18727, 100.44697, 100.52…
annual_data <- economic_data |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  ) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    hourly_wage = mean(hourly_wage, na.rm = TRUE),
    cpi = mean(cpi, na.rm = TRUE),
    wage_index = mean(wage_index, na.rm = TRUE),
    price_index = mean(price_index, na.rm = TRUE),
    real_wage_index = mean(real_wage_index, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

annual_data
wage_price_plot_data <- annual_data |>
  select(
    year,
    wage_index,
    price_index
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(wage_index, price_index),
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "index"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    series = recode(
      series,
      wage_index = "Nominal hourly wage",
      price_index = "Consumer prices"
    )
  )
p1 <- ggplot(
  wage_price_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = index,
    linetype = series
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Wages and Prices Since 2015",
    subtitle = "2015 average = 100",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Index (2015 = 100)",
    linetype = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 2015:2025
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p1

ggsave(
  "../figures/wages_vs_prices.png",
  p1,
  width = 9,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
p2 <- ggplot(
  annual_data,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = real_wage_index
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 100,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Real Hourly Wages Since 2015",
    subtitle = "Nominal wages adjusted for consumer prices; 2015 = 100",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Real Wage Index (2015 = 100)"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 2015:2025
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p2

ggsave(
  "../figures/real_wage_index.png",
  p2,
  width = 9,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
calculate_growth <- function(start_year, end_year, period_name) {

  start <- annual_data |>
    filter(year == start_year)

  end <- annual_data |>
    filter(year == end_year)

  tibble(
    period = period_name,

    nominal_wage_growth =
      (end$hourly_wage / start$hourly_wage - 1) * 100,

    price_growth =
      (end$cpi / start$cpi - 1) * 100,

    real_wage_growth =
      (end$real_wage_index / start$real_wage_index - 1) * 100
  )
}
period_growth <- bind_rows(
  calculate_growth(
    2015,
    2019,
    "2015–2019"
  ),
  calculate_growth(
    2019,
    2022,
    "2019–2022"
  ),
  calculate_growth(
    2022,
    2025,
    "2022–2025"
  )
)

period_growth
period_plot_data <- period_growth |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      nominal_wage_growth,
      price_growth,
      real_wage_growth
    ),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "growth"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    measure = recode(
      measure,
      nominal_wage_growth = "Nominal wage growth",
      price_growth = "Price growth",
      real_wage_growth = "Real wage growth"
    )
  )
p3 <- ggplot(
  period_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = period,
    y = growth,
    fill = measure
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = "dodge"
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Wage Growth, Inflation, and Purchasing Power",
    subtitle = "Percent change across three periods",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percent Change (%)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p3
